reference.title: Dumbbell Seated Calf Raise
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Calves, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the heels rise, inhale as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.8 s pause, 1.8 s down

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbells, then balls of the feet on a plate or step for a deeper stretch, then single-leg

cues.text: Sit on the end of the bench, feet flat a little wider than the hips, shins vertical; lay a dumbbell across each lower thigh just behind the knee and hold it there.
Breathe out and press through the balls of the feet, lifting the heels and the dumbbells as high as you can.
Pause at the top; weight over the big and second toes, ankles straight (no rolling out).
Breathe in and lower the heels slowly to the floor.
Touch down without bouncing and repeat.

mistakes.fix: Full range: heels all the way down, pause at the top, slow lowering.

mistakes.mistake: Feet rolling out onto the little toes
mistakes.fix: Keep the pressure on the big and second toes.

mistakes.mistake: Pushing the dumbbells up with the arms
mistakes.fix: The hands only hold the dumbbells in place; the calves lift them.
Shins vertical, knees over the ankles, so the load sits over the balls of the feet.

kinematics.norm: Full range from heels down to as high as possible; the seated knee-90 position biases the soleus (Kinoshita 2023)
Lift as high as possible each rep (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees, as in the seated training condition of Kinoshita 2023; the knee rises with the heel
Across the lower thighs just behind the knees, held in place by the hands (common setup; clinical opinion)
About 1-2 s up and 2 s down; Kinoshita 2023 trained at 2 s up, 2 s down

Hébert-Losier, Schneiders, García, Sullivan & Simoneau 2012, influence of knee flexion angle and age on triceps surae muscle fatigue during heel raises (J Strength Cond Res 26(11))

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or cramping occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Rest the dumbbells on the thigh muscle just behind the kneecap, not on the kneecap itself.
modify: Achilles or plantar heel pain: smaller range and lighter load, slow tempo.
Knee discomfort under the dumbbells: fold a towel over the thighs.
progressions: Balls of the feet on a plate or step for a deeper stretch.
Single-leg seated raise with one heavier dumbbell.

muscleNotes.calves_r: Soleus-biased plantarflexion: with the knee bent 90 degrees the two-joint gastrocnemius is slack. In a 12-week trial seated (knee 90 degrees) calf raises grew the soleus as much as standing raises (2.9% vs 2.1%) but barely changed the gastrocnemius (0.6-1.7% vs 9-12% standing; Kinoshita 2023).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Soleus-biased plantarflexion: with the knee bent 90 degrees the two-joint gastrocnemius is slack. In a 12-week trial seated (knee 90 degrees) calf raises grew the soleus as much as standing raises (2.9% vs 2.1%) but barely changed the gastrocnemius (0.6-1.7% vs 9-12% standing; Kinoshita 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip holds the dumbbells in place across the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip holds the dumbbells in place across the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall on the bench (clinical opinion).
